newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR APRIL 14 - DEC 31, 1997.
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR APRIL 14 - DEC 31, 1997.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands hosts summit of European Union leaders (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13).
BRUSSELS - Conference of Bosnian donor countries originally scheduled for April has been POSTPONED to an unspecified date before June.
MONDAY, APRIL 14
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Fisheries Council (To April 15).
Agenda includes:

- Proposal for a Council decision on objectives and detailed rules for restructuring the Community fisheries sector for the period from 1 January 1997 to 31 December 1999 with a view to achieving a balance on a sustainable basis between resources and their exploitation (MAGPs IV).
- Proposal for a Council regulation on autonomous Community tariff quotas for certain fishery products.

- Proposal for a Council regulation on amendment of regulation (CE) No 390197 fixing, for certain stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1997 and certain conditions under which they may be fished (allocation of Atlanto-Scandian herring and horse mackerel).
- Proposal for a Council decision on specific measure to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities.
- Other business:
- Report from the Commission on the application of the Community system for fisheries and aquaculture;
- Oral presentation by the Commission on fisheries agreements - Current situation and perspectives;
- Reflection paper by the Spanish delegation on drift-nets.

LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Finnish Justice Minister Kari Haekaemies meets Court of Justice President Gil Carlos Rodriguez Iglesias at 1130/0930 GMT; discussions focus on the organisation and role of the Court of Justice in the context of the inter-governmental conference and the need for cooperation between the Court of Justice and the national legal systems of the member states - followed by a news conference at 1600/1400 GMT. Contact: Tom Kennedy (352) 4303 3355.
LEIDEN, Netherlands - The Philip Morris Institute (PMI) holds conference on "How much popular support is there for he EU?". Contact: PMI (322) 732 1156.
TUESDAY, APRIL 15

BRUSSELS - Inuit Circumpolar Conference holds conference on "Wildlife management, indigenous peoples and the world of politics" (1000/0800 GMT). Topics discussed are the objectives of import bans and international trading obligations: the case of EU import prohibitions; indigenous peoples' concerns with animal welfare and trade restrictions; the objectives of animal welfare groups and the realities of wildlife management; sustainability and the realities of life. Venue: EP, Belliard room 53. Contact: Inuit Circumpolar Conference, Greenland (299) 2 36 32.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds workshop on "Identifying the priorities for energy conservation" (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes: myths and realities in energy conservation: what is really needed; energy conservation in business: potentials and obstacles; the impacts of liberalisation on energy efficiency and renewables; integration of climate change objectives; how the necessary long-term consensus on climate change policy can be established. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - The European Energy Foundation holds dinner debate on "Medium and long term security of supply of oil and gas in Europe" (1900/1700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Europa. Contact: The European Energy Foundation (322) 773 9522.
VALETTA, Malta - EU and Mediterranean ministers attend Euro-Med conference in a follow-up to the 1995 Barcelona conference (To April 16).
MOSCOW (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov to discuss next round of talks for NATO/Russia charter.

ATHENS (NEW ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) President Tom Jenkins meets Greek President Costas Simitis; discussions focus on socio-professional contribution to the European decision-making process and on ECOSOC in the institutional architecture at the dawn of the inter-governmental conference - followed by a joint news conference at 1345/1145 GMT.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 16
BRUSSELS - EP and Council Conciliation Committee meets on "TV without frontiers directive".

MAASTRICHT - The National Committee for International Cooperation and Sustainable Development and the Dutch foreign affairs ministry host conference on "Public support for international cooperation" (To April 17).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Norway-Outside of the EU" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is Ambassador of Norway to the EU Einar Bull. Venue: CPES. Contact: CEPS (322) 3911.

BRUSSELS - Schleswig-Holstein Economics, Technology and Transport Minister Peer Steinbrueck addresses the fourth maritime dialogue conference on "Short sea shipping in the Baltic Sea - Importance and development of transport chains" (1800/1600 GMT). Venue: House of the new German Laender, 80 Blvd Saint Michel. Contact: House of the new German Laender (322) 285 4657.
BRUSSELS - Aeronautica holds "European air transport conference" (To April 17). Venue: Sheraton Towers. Contact: Aeronautica (44) 181 893 3795.
THURSDAY, APRIL 17
LUXEMBOURG - Social Affairs Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Employment and Labour Market Committee.
- Modified proposal for a directive on "Chemical Agents".
- Worker information and consultation.
- (possibly) Commission activities on analysis, research, cooperation and action in the field of employment.
- (possibly) Directive modifying directive 90/394/CEE concerning the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
- (possibly) New communication on the future of social protection.
- (possibly) White Paper on working time in excluded sectors.
- Proposal for a directive: "Burden of proof in cases of discrimination based on sex".

- Proposal for a directive amending directive 76/207/EEC on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women as regards access to employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions (Kalanke Ruling).
- Collective redundancies (Codification).
- Council Recommendation on home working.
MAASTRICHT - Dutch EU presidency hosts post-Lome ministerial meeting (April 18).

BRUSSELS - Katholieke Universiteit Brussel (KU) holds international relations lecture on "Mixed signals: Central bank independence, wage bargaining". Speaker is Harvard University Government Professor Peter Hall. Venue: KU Brussels. Contact: KU (322) 412 4211.
FRIDAY, APRIL 18
AMSTERDAM - Informal Environment Council (To April 20). No agenda yet available.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Committee for Banking Standards (ECBS) holds news conference at 1200/1000 GMT. Venue: ECBS offices, 12 avenue de Tervuren. Contact: ECBS (322)733 3533.

BOLOGNA, Italy (NEW ITEM) - European Commission and Committee of the Regions hold joint seminar on "Climate change, energy and strategic response at local and regional level" (0830/0630 GMT). Venue: Piazza Maggiore 6. Contact: Comunicatori Associati (39) 51 276211.

MAASTRICHT - Dutch Development Cooperation Minister Jan Pronk hosts meeting on the future of the Lome convention, which lays down the political, trade and aid relations between the EU and the 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific states (To April 19). Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 2/8 - Apr 21-May 10)
MONDAY, APRIL 21
LUXEMBOURG - Farm Council (To April 22). No agenda yet available.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Uganda President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addresses Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) meeting on "National resistance movement's vision, philosophy and governance of Uganda: experience and the way ahead" (1830/1630 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

MALTA - European Documentation and Research Centre (EDRC) and University of Malta hold "The State of the European Union Conference 1997". Discussions focus on the development of EU policies, especially with regard to the EU citizens' ombudsman; the evolution of cooperation on justice and home affairs in Europe; EU social policy; EU initiatives for employment and growth and the EU's SME policy. Contact: Monica Cauchi, EDRC (356) 32 90 20 01.
TUESDAY, APRIL 22
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0800 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Van Miert gives address on "The European Commission's view on competition policy and public aids" (1215/1015 GMT). Venue: FEB, 4 rue Ravenstein. Contact: Christine Legrand, FEB (322) 515 0826.

BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To April 24).

THURSDAY, APRIL 24

Provisional agenda includes:

a) (possibly) Individual cases of state aid;

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Lithuania and the EU" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is Ambassador of Lithuania to the EU Jonas Cicinskas. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 3911.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Innovative research and appropriate health care for the people of Europe" (To April 25).

THE HAGUE (EXPANDED ITEM) - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Trafficking in women" (To April 26). The conference aims to bring about recommendations for a code of conduct to prevent and combat trafficking in women. It is a follow-up to the fourth world women's conference in Beijing in 1995 and the European conference on trafficking in women held in Vienna in 1996. Discussion topics include the prevention, detection and prosecution of those involved in trafficking in women, and help for the victims. Participants include: European Commissioner Gradin, Austrian Women's Issues Minister Barbara Prammer, Dutch Employment and Social Affairs Minister Ad Melkert, Dutch Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager.
SATURDAY, APRIL 26
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - NATO Chief of Defence Staff meets to examine and (possibly) adopt a reform of NATO's command structure.
MONDAY, APRIL 28

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts "European cohesion forum" (1430/1230 GMT) (To April 30). Speakers include: European Commission President Santer, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles, Committee of the Regions President Pasquall Maragall, ECOSOC President Tom Jenkins, European Commissioners Wulf-Mathies, Flynn and Fischler. Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: Mr Scheins (322) 295 1409.

SATURDAY, MAY 10

THURSDAY, MAY 15
